#### 1. catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.775)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2672351, Reactome:R-HSA-5578775)

**Proposed mechanism:** RYR2 mutation (null) —DISRUPTS→ RYR2 (HGNC:10484); RYR2 (HGNC:10484) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac calcium handling (GO:0003010); Cardiac calcium handling (GO:0003010) —LEADS_TO→ Ventricular tachycardia (HP:0011677); Cardiac calcium handling (GO:0003010) —LEADS_TO→ Catecholamine-induced arrhythmias (HP:0030773). Gain-of-function mutations in the RYR2 gene disrupt normal cardiac calcium handling, leading to aberrant calcium release and subsequent development of ventricular tachycardia and catecholamine-induced arrhythmias in both CPVT and CPVT1.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in genes other than RYR2, CASQ2, TRDN, CALM1, CALM3, or TECRL that are exclusively associated with one of the two disease phenotypes would falsify the hypothesis of a shared RYR2-centric mechanism. _(variant: Exclusion of known pathogenic RYR2 variants from gnomAD populations at frequencies greater than 1% would support their pathogenicity.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared RYR2 mechanism in CPVT and CPVT1 provides a common therapeutic target. Strategies aimed at stabilizing RYR2 function, such as beta-blockers or novel modulators of calcium handling, could potentially benefit patients with both conditions.
